RescheduleAppointmentRequest.description: Fresh admission facts for the new time. externalReferences must be omitted; the appointment retains the immutable set established by its hold or direct booking.

bearerAuth.description: A fresh access token from the configured issuer, for this deployment's audience, signed by a key the issuer published. Catalogue, availability, and ordinary owned-record reads demand the configured reads scope (scheduling:read by default); the explain path demands the configured explain scope (scheduling:explain by default), which is never the reads scope. Source-manager detail accepts appointment.read with the exact retained manager and service/location binding and fresh online status, without a general reads scope. The operational work list demands exactly one explicitly configured operational profile; catalogue scopes and task grants never authorize it. A mutating route demands no scope at all: its authority is the complete task grant the token carries, whose scheduling permissions the service checks against the offering's service and location and the action the route performs (hold.create, hold.release, appointment.create, appointment.reschedule, appointment.cancel, attendance.record). Source-managed creation instead uses hold.create-for or appointment.create-for and always checks fresh online status. A token with partial grant claims is refused rather than half-trusted.

info.description: Implemented Scheduling HTTP contract: published openings, exact-time offerings over interchangeable resource pools, published arrival windows with channel subquotas, holds, and accountable bookings. Mutating authority is a complete task grant; every refusal is one problem from the closed vocabulary.

post.description: Carries exactly one of hold or admission. Confirming transfers the hold's own reservation: the hold must still be active and unexpired, its policy revision still current, and its owner or source-manager binding must match. Exact-time confirmation also checks current physical supply: the selected resource still exists, carries the required capabilities, is available over the entire occupied interval, and satisfies the offering's current opening coverage. It does not re-run new-request start-grid, lead-time or horizon rules for an already admitted hold. A direct create is evaluated against the live ledger like a hold, and commits instead of reserving. Both branches demand a complete task grant naming the offering's service, location, and appointment.create. Source-managed creation or confirmation instead requires appointment.create-for, the same verified manager binding and fresh online grant status.

get.description: An ordinary booking requires its retained actor owner and reads scope, or a current appointment.read task grant for its retained service/location. A source-managed booking additionally requires the signed source-manager binding to match its retained manager. Both grant paths require fresh online grant status, need no general reads scope, and grant no catalogue, list or history access. The grant is scoped to service/location (and manager where applicable), not to an appointment identifier. A booking outside that authority, a hold, and an unknown identifier are all operation.not-authorized, so existence outside the caller's authority is never disclosed.

put.description: Requires attendance.record for the appointment's stored service and location. Both observedAppointmentRevision and observedRevision must match the locked current visit; observedRevision is zero before that visit's first observation. Corrections advance the attendance revision without changing the booking revision or capacity. Rescheduling starts a new visit; cancellation preserves the existing visit and permits later observations. observedAt cannot be in the future. The observation applies to the appointment, including a resource-only booking, and never invents a person count. Neither ownership, a read scope, nor an operational profile authorizes this write. Exact idempotent replay returns the original observation.

get.description: The public view of the authored policy, sorted by identifier. Exact-time offerings carry durationMinutes, bufferBeforeMinutes, bufferAfterMinutes, startIncrementMinutes, and maxRecipients. An offering that accepts caller-selected durations publishes durationSelection; one that accepts a named resource publishes its pool and allowResourceSelection. Non-default occupied-interval opening coverage is explicit. An arrival-window offering that names its window carries window; one that names none carries windows, every records-published window it serves in start order, and a request, hold or reschedule picks one of them by its start. A field the offering's mode does not use is null, never zero.

post.description: Atomically applies a bounded snapshot under expectedRevision and a canonical request digest, preserving facts outside the source authority and coverage. After an uncertain reply, replay the exact body and expectedRevision: retained exact replay returns already-applied. A different stale request returns HTTP 412 revision.mismatch. A later conflict does not establish that an earlier attempt failed. There is no Idempotency-Key header and clients do not retry automatically. Unavailable or expired required-source coverage prevents new allocations without cancelling existing commitments. Input bounds and minimized impact projection match preview.

post.description: Reports replacement effects within the selected source, resources and coverage. Coverage is bounded to 62 days, 256 resources and 4096 records; each interval must lie inside coverage. Identifiers are bounded in UTF-8 bytes (512 for externalUid, 256 for externalRevision) and cannot contain control characters. Fresh snapshots require freshUntil after observedAt within the configured freshness bound; unavailable snapshots have no records or freshUntil and preserve known busy intervals. Existing commitments remain unchanged. Impact detail is absent by default; an explicitly enabled profile can expose only kind, resource and occupied interval. This read reserves no capacity.
